t: For necessary expenses to carry out motor carrier safety functions of the Secretaiy, as authorized by the Department of Transportation Act (80 Stat. 939–40), $13,700,000, of which $3,800,000 of the amount appropriated herein shall remain available until expended and not to exceed $1,264,000 shall be available for “Limitation on general operating expenses”.

fable.w: This is a plain appropriation that funds the Secretary's motor carrier safety functions and sets limits on how long and for what the money is available. The tempting reading is that "motor carrier safety functions" implies regulating or dealing with outside carriers, but the text creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: For necessary expenses to carry out motor carrier safety functions of the Secretaiy, as authorized by the Department of Transportation Act (80 Stat. 939–40), $13,700,000

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that allocates funds for the Secretary's motor carrier safety functions. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, nor does it create advisory bodies, public comment periods, or rights to sue. It merely specifies budgetary amounts and limitations.
qwen_block.s: For necessary expenses to carry out motor carrier safety functions of the Secretaiy, as authorized by the Department of Transportation Act (80 Stat. 939–40), $13,700,000, of which $3,800,000 of the amount appropriated herein shall remain available until expended and not to exceed $1,264,000 shall be available for “Limitation on general operating expenses”.

opus.w: This section only provides funding for the Secretary's motor carrier safety functions and sets limits on how the money can be used. The mention of safety functions might suggest regulatory activity, but the text sets up no rulemaking, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
opus.s: For necessary expenses to carry out motor carrier safety functions of the Secretaiy, as authorized by the Department of Transportation Act (80 Stat. 939–40), $13,700,000
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** "Motor carrier safety functions" might suggest regulation, and regulation can involve the public. But this section only sets aside money and says how long it stays available. It does not require rulemaking, a hearing, consultation, an advisory body or any other way for people outside the federal government to take part in a decision. Like Example 1, it is just funding.
